issue.title: test_sudo_answer_defers_after_long_lock_timeout_and_reclaim_settles_later settles instead of deferring when the lock holder self-releases under load

task_type_fields.evidence:
Proposed by sase-1oj.4 note #1 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: "the remaining sudo settlement timeout has no matching bead found"); triaged by the sase-1oj land agent.

**Observations (machine-local ToolRun failure group c0d9ad62…, `check / test (scoped)`):** 3 failing `just check` runs across 2 agents and 2 workspaces between 2026-10-24 and 2026-10-26, including ToolRuns `5721d601c1ba2453537c837556798089` (sase-1oj.4) and `e4eb24b4a49956722b5849e1666692f0`. In both inspected logs the call phase took ~63 s and failed at `tests/test_sudo_ledger_settlement.py:370`:

```
>       assert payload["settlement"] == "deferred"
E       AssertionError: assert 'settled' == 'deferred'
```

**Passes serially:** `pytest tests/test_sudo_ledger_settlement.py` passed on master 8d41b72218 (apollo, load ~8) during the sase-1oj landing.

**Likely root cause:** the helper thread holds the gate follow-up lock only until `release_lock.wait(timeout=2)` expires, then releases it on its own. Under a loaded parallel lane `_apply_sudo_receipt` reaches its lock attempt more than 2 s after `lock_held` is set (the whole call took 63 s). The lock is free by then, so settlement completes as `settled` instead of `deferred`. Suggested fix: keep the holder until the test explicitly sets `release_lock`, with a generous safety timeout (e.g. 60 s), and keep the existing `join`/`is_alive` assertions. Do not weaken the `deferred` assertion.
